explanation: No clear shared feature. Fires on assorted tokens, often function words (to, the, it, this) in questions or uncertain clauses ('how to', 'would it', 'Could this be the'), plus unrelated word fragments (-ut in micronutrient, -ft in engraft) and code/SPARQL tokens.

Fires on a middle subword piece inside rare proper names and foreign words that are split into several tokens (Sh-ann-ons, Eö-tv-ös, Ben-G-urion, T-eg-ucigalpa, Mark Ham-ill), especially non-English names and places. Common English words and punctuation give little or no activation.

Mixture. Fires on the tag name right after ', , , , ). It also fires on prose tokens that are dependent heads in phrases such as 'given', 'difficult to', 'needed to', 'result of', 'challenge for' and 'To that end', which share no obvious feature with the HTML tags.

Loosely fires on closing or separator tokens in structured text, such as ' </' and '</' that start closing XML/HTML tags, commas in dates, semicolons, and '");'. It also fires on scattered prose and chemistry fragments, so it is not specific to any one of these.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that is split across tokens, mostly in non-English (French, German, Portuguese, Romanian, Danish) text: ' déf', ' P', 'ü', ' ap', ' tr', ' termin'. Also fires moderately on capitalized word-initial pieces in English (' Sk', '-Pro'). Whole common words give weak activation.

Mixture. Fires most on a '0' inside a long run of zeros and on ' file' in license-header boilerplate ('This file is part of'). It also fires on assorted word-internal fragments (-cept, -vest, -ild, -ow) and on a few plural nouns, with no clear common thread.

Fires mainly on software-license boilerplate in code headers: 'with' in 'in compliance with the License', 'LICENSE' in file references, 'distributed', 'Version', ', free of charge'. Outside license text, fires more weakly on assorted nouns (option, border, storage).

Fires on words about machines or systems operating: verbs and nouns of running, operation and conditions ('operating under a heavy load', 'turn on', 'would run 24 hours', 'pump falls below', 'operating frequency', 'input/output' in R Shiny servers). Mostly in technical or patent-style prose about engines, pumps and devices.

Mixture of unrelated contexts. Fires on code tokens ('import (' in generated Go files, '.php', 'supertest', 'package' after a license header) and on parts of proper names and places ('Rio de Janeiro', 'Oslo', 'Trayvon Martin', the second part of surnames).

Fires on the later subword pieces of abbreviations, acronyms and split names (PU-F, H-cy, CLE-VEL-AND, SS-SI, ED-DP), and also on ''s' in 'one's'. Scattered other tokens (age group, train of) also activate it. Loosely: the continuation of a fragmented token.

Fires on the middle or final subword pieces of long technical biomedical or materials-science compound terms (semi-conductor, paraff-in, dodecyl sulfate, sarcoplasm-ic, glomer-ular, plasmin-ogen, lip-op-rotein). Usually inside multi-word scientific names of molecules, tissues or devices.

Two groups. (1) Grant, funding and application language: 'claims the benefit', 'CAREER award', 'career development', 'This project was funded', 'visa', 'Deferred Action'. (2) Pieces of cytokine and growth-factor names (chem-ok-ine, SC-F, VEG-F, growth factor, interleukin-2). Both are biomedical-research or administrative vocabulary.

No clear common feature. Fires on varied tokens in code (Context, (int), offset =, Math.round, commas in argument lists), on chemistry and medical word fragments (sub-jug-ation, intramus-cular, acetal-dehyde), and on prose function words. Commas and list separators show up somewhat often.

Fires on structural break tokens in short-line, list-like text: double newlines between short items in tables, menus or headers, colons that introduce a list or explanation, '**' in math or markdown, and a sentence-initial 'There'. Strongest where text is fragmented into short items.

Fires on a middle subword piece of a long word split into several tokens (recom-enda-ção, er-stat-ninger, Nanoc-aps-ules, plurip-ot-ency, remb-ourse-ment). Common in Romance and Germanic languages and in scientific terms, and on capitalized fragments in all-caps legal text.

Fires on a piece of a technical or scientific compound term that follows a prefix or modifier: 'in situ hybrid(ization)', 'gas chromat(ography)', 'X-ray', 'photos-ensitive', 'surface-mount', 'immunos-orbent'. Typical of laboratory-method and patent text. A few prose tokens ('among', 'Against') activate it as unrelated exceptions.

Mixture. Fires on the suffix 'ability' in tolerability and acceptability, on 'groups' in subgroups, on 'temple', and on assorted nouns and verb particles (shrinking, away, lion, flares, ritual). No unifying feature is clear.

Fires on speech and reporting verbs, 'said', 'say' and 'says', especially right after a named speaker in news-style attribution ('Sean Payton said', 'PG&E said', 'we say', 'can honestly say'). Moderate on other reporting or cognition verbs (found, mean, telling, announcing, hope).

Fires on a word-internal subword piece of a word split into fragments, often in non-English text (Estonian, Spanish, Russian, Norwegian) or rare terms (kallik-re-in, Mujah-ide-en, anti-counter-fe-iting, disple-asure). Usually the second or middle piece. Whole common words do not activate it.

Fires on the word-initial piece 'pro' / 'Pro' / 'prof' / 'prov' / 'prost' (Profuse, prophylaxis, Proximity, Pro Bowl, Protesters, prosthesis, profanity), in any language or context. Moderate on fuller 'pro-' words such as proportion, product, projection and profile.

No clear common feature. Fires on varied tokens: code and URL punctuation (size_t, ':' in an ARN, '://'), prepositions and articles (from, in, of, at, with, a), and foreign-language word endings (degli, -ší, -ás).
